wv_long_wall_the.blurb: A bolted-only wall beside Summersville Lake, in the Gauley River country of the New River Gorge region. Roughly two dozen sport lines on sandstone, with the weight of the grades sitting in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, a handful of 5.9 and 5.10 routes for warming up, and a couple of very easy pitches. The lake crags as a group suit a wide spread of abilities, but this particular wall is best for climbers already comfortable leading in the 5.10s and above. Summer trails around the lake are home to copperheads, so watch your step.

wv_long_branch_wall.blurb: A tall limestone buttress in Smoke Hole Canyon, in the Monongahela National Forest of eastern West Virginia. About two dozen routes, mostly bolted with a few that want trad gear. Grades start around 5.7 and 5.8, with a solid middle of 5.10 to 5.12 and one or two at the very top end. The wall holds some of the longest and most technical lines in the canyon, a mix of precise face moves and steeper short pitches, plus a few moderates for climbers who are not at their limit.

wv_6_butcher_s_branch.blurb: A well-liked sport sector on the rim of the New River Gorge at Kaymoor, near Fayetteville. Around two dozen routes on sandstone, mostly bolted with a few trad lines. The range goes from an easy 5.6 and some long, sustained 5.9s up through a deep batch of 5.10 to 5.12 climbs, with the bulk of the routes at 5.11 and 5.12. The face stays cool through the summer, which makes it a hot-weather choice, though it seeps for a day or so after rain and can feel busy on good days.

wv_bear_rocks_preserve.blurb: A small bouldering area at the north end of the Dolly Sods plateau in eastern West Virginia, at roughly 3,900 feet. About two dozen problems are scattered among a jumble of outcrops beside the road, grouped into a few little clusters. The grades lean easy to moderate, mostly V0 to V3, with a few at V4 and one harder problem. The terrain is open and exposed, and the weather up on the plateau can turn rough, so it suits a short session on a clear day rather than a full-day tour. Views across the Allegheny Front are a bonus.

wv_sunset_wall.blurb: A short cliff in Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia, a few minutes on foot from the main lot past the climbers kiosk. At about 20 to 30 feet it is the forest's most popular top-rope wall, split by a chimney, with a few lines that also take a standard trad rack. Sandstone throughout. Most of the sixteen or so top-rope routes fall between 5.9 and 5.11, with a smaller number of harder and easier ones, and a few V0 to V2 boulder problems sit alongside. Good for beginners and groups; big trees above provide anchors.
wv_sunset_wall.approach: From the main lot, follow the trail past the climbers kiosk and the roadside boulders. The cliff appears on your left after a few minutes.
